inconsistencies: #36628 and #36608 are the same rewrite: #36628 is the base (it states it unblocks #36608) and #36608 adds package relay plus the bitcoin-privbcast tool on top. Review #36628 first; they should not be reviewed as independent proposals.

The private broadcast rewrite (#36628/#36608) deletes the subsystem that #34533, #36330, #36607, #36477, #34322 and #34271 patch. A direction decision on the rewrite should come before heavy review investment in the incremental fixes.

#34533 and #36330 are competing fixes for the same leak (wallet rebroadcast under -privatebroadcast deanonymising the node): one routes rebroadcasts through private broadcast, the other suppresses resubmission. They must be decided together; #36607 is a backstop for the same failure class and only makes sense after that decision.
#36506 depends on #36437 and re-fixes the announcer-disconnect orphan hole; #36437 must be reviewed and merged first.
#36506 also fixes the txid==wtxid orphan-request wiping that #36486 addresses independently. Review #36506 first and then decide whether #36486 is still needed.
#36787 is the stated prerequisite for #35558 (prefill series); merge order is #36787 then #35558 even though #35558 carries the measurable benefit.
#36607 depends on #36477 retaining finished private broadcast records; #36477 is banded lower than its dependent and should still be reviewed first.
#36244, #36445 and #35561 all reduce cs_main acquisition in net_processing and will conflict. #36445 is self-contained and measured; #36244 subsumes much of the same ground.
#35502 (receive side) and #35522 (send side) are the same move-only extraction exercise in net_processing and will conflict with #34824 and #36244; sequence them after the behavioural work.
#30988 (Split CConnman) and #35040 (part of the #33958 net/net_processing split) are two concurrent architectural splits of the same code; they need coordination before either is reviewed in depth.
#36727 contains only commits already merged to master; it carries no unresolved p2p problem and is a release-branch mechanism.
result.notes: Two clusters dominate the top of this category and should be triaged as units rather than as individual PRs: private broadcast origin privacy (#36628/#36608 rewrite versus the incremental #34533/#36330/#36607/#36477/#34322 fixes) and 1p1c package relay liveness (#36015, #36437, #36506, #36486, #36328). Outside those, P1 is reserved for remotely exploitable resource exhaustion and origin-privacy breaks; concrete DoS, connectivity and interoperability fixes sit in P2; and the large pool of P3 work is addrman/configuration hygiene, refactors and tests.
